title: Environmental and energy performance assessment of a methanol–diesel RCCI engine through explainable machine learning
content:
Abstract

The transition toward sustainable transportation requires cleaner combustion technologies capable of improving efficiency while reducing environmental impacts. This study experimentally investigates the combustion, performance, and emission characteristics of a methanol–diesel Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI) engine equipped with a Common Rail Direct Injection (CRDI) system. Experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder Kirloskar TV1 engine at injection pressures of 400–600 bar and injection timings of 21°–25° BTDC under full-load operation. Methanol was supplied through port fuel injection to create a partially premixed charge, while diesel was directly injected as the high-reactivity fuel. RCCI operation improved brake thermal efficiency to 29.8%, while reducing brake-specific fuel consumption, CO, UHC, and smoke emissions; among tested conditions, the best performance was achieved at 23° BTDC and 500 bars. However, NO x emissions increased with higher in-cylinder temperatures, reflecting the well-known efficiency–NO x trade-off in RCCI combustion. Net environmental benefit therefore depends on how this trade-off is weighted, and on factors beyond the present scope such as after-treatment and methanol production pathway. Among five machine learning models developed for performance prediction, Support Vector Regression achieved the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.9696), while SHAP analysis provided interpretable insights into parameter influence. The findings demonstrate the potential of RCCI and explainable artificial intelligence to support cleaner energy systems and contribute to Sustainable Development Goals SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
